title: Tesla unveils its new Roadster sports car, which can thrust itself into the air
source_used: NBC News (the AP video page returned HTTP 403)
key_facts: Elon Musk showed a Tesla Roadster prototype on Thursday (15 Oct) at a SpaceX testing facility in Texas, eight years after the car was first announced.
Musk told the live audience that what they were about to see 'was not AI or SI'.
The car slowly drove up a curved ramp shaped like half of a roller coaster loop, launched, cleared five other Tesla vehicles and landed softly in a cloud of condensation using cold-gas thrusters.
Musk after the stunt: 'Well, it worked!', adding that 'it's not necessarily a safety-optimized car'.
A second run jumped 27 feet in the air with a barrel roll, according to Tesla.
Tesla says it reached 0-60 mph in 0.81 seconds, more than a second faster than the discontinued Model S Plaid.
Tesla says a fan-based suction system creates downforce to hold the car against the road, and self-refilling cold-gas thrusters power its airborne moves.

Three versions: Performance (road-ready, suction system, no thrusters), Thrust (race-ready, adds rear-mounted thrusters), Rocket (air-ready, invite-only, one seat, cold-gas thrusters along the perimeter), according to Tesla.
No price or release date has been announced; Musk said production would not begin until 2028.
Musk acknowledged the Roadster might not be legal in every jurisdiction; Tesla says the Rocket version is not approved for public roads.
The second-generation Roadster was first unveiled in 2017, with Musk promising production in 2020; Tesla has pushed the date back repeatedly while still taking reservations.

Musk wants the car to 'crack halfway to the speed of sound', about 383 mph, more than 150 mph above the current announced top speed, and says it will go 300 miles on one charge, less than half of what he first promised (said for when it is released).
Buyers can reserve the base model for a $50,000 deposit, or $250,000 for the Thrust version.
quote_evidence: Elon Musk showed off a new vehicle prototype Thursday that can briefly launch itself into the air using rocket-inspired thrusters.
The company has yet to announce a price or release date, though the Tesla and SpaceX CEO said production would not begin until 2028.
Minutes later, it sped away with a 0.81-second 0-60 mph time, according to Tesla, which is more than a second faster than the company’s current fastest time with the now-discontinued Model S Plaid.
“Well, it worked!” Musk said after the stunt, adding that “it’s not necessarily a safety-optimized car.”
Moments later, the car accelerated toward the same five cars and jumped 27 feet in the air, according to Tesla, while performing a barrel roll.
Tesla says a fan-based suction system creates downforce to hold the vehicle against the road’s surface, while self-refilling cold-gas thrusters power its airborne maneuvers.
Musk acknowledged the Roadster might not be legal in every jurisdiction, while Tesla says the Rocket version is not approved for public roads.
Prospective buyers can reserve the base model for an initial deposit of $50,000, or $250,000 for the Thrust augment.
why_it_matters_hint: A long-delayed car shown with thruster stunts, but with no price, no date and legal questions for the flying version.
